Hi Thiago — thanks for the heads up. Short answers up front, then details below so your treasury team can pick the cleanest path.

Preferred rail: local BRL credit into our Brazilian collections account (nostro) — this avoids correspondent conversion spreads and makes reconciliation straightforward.
If local BRL is not possible: instruct your bank to use SHA (sender pays their own outgoing charges, beneficiary pays any beneficiary-side fees). We accept SHA for most customers, but please note Redwood will not automatically accept a reduced/net payment unless pre-approved.
If your team insists on OUR (sender covers all intermediaries) we can accept that but please confirm in advance; Redwood Finance requires copies of the SWIFT/MT103 to reconcile intermediary charges for reimbursement. Reimbursement policy: we can reimburse documented correspondent fees up to USD 50 equivalent per payment after review. Anything above needs pre-approval.

Wire instructions (stub — see attached redwood_wire_instructions_v2.pdf for full):
- Beneficiary name: Redwood Inference Limited (BRL Collections)
- Bank: Banco do Brasil S.A.

VAT note: Redwood is not VAT-registered in Brazil for local withholding purposes on this technical services invoice; treat this as cross-border SaaS export. Please include your remittance metadata exactly as Invoice_2027-08-FC12345.pdf to avoid tax reclassification on our side. If your tax team insists on VAT handling, please send the proposed remittance text and we will loop Legal.

Attachments: redwood_wire_instructions_v2.pdf (contains nostro/nostro fallback rails and USD correspondent fallback instructions).

Let me know which rail your treasury chooses and we'll confirm acceptance (and whether we need to do a quick pre-approval for reimbursement).

Hi Thiago, Laura — looping in the Collections/FX side. A few points to make treasury workflows consistent and avoid reconciliation rework: 

- Preference order: (1) Local BRL to our Banco do Brasil account (preferred), (2) USD routed to our USD nostro with instructions OUR (only if your bank cannot send BRL), (3) GBP as last resort.
- If you route USD via correspondent and choose OUR: Redwood Finance will reimburse *documented* correspondent charges after settlement. Reimbursement policy: up to USD 50 per payment (this cap is per payment, not per intermediary). We need the MT103 and the incoming bank's affirmation of the fee (bank statement or confirmation email) to process reimbursement. Please attach PDF copies to the wire ticket in HubSpot (HubSpot-Deal-54321).
- If you send SHA: your outgoing fees will be billed by your bank; Redwood will not top up to make you whole. Beneficiary-side receiving fees (applied by our receiving bank) will be deducted from the credited amount unless previously agreed. If you cannot tolerate deductions, use OUR and we will reimburse within the cap above after evidence.
- Net payments: Redwood cannot accept net/net (i.e., paying less than the invoice amount without prior written approval). If treasury's system only supports netting, please have your payments team reach out 48 hours in advance so we can issue a pre-approved credit note.
- FX spread: Redwood will not reimburse any FX spread taken by your bank when converting USD->BRL. Reimbursement covers only explicit correspondent/intermediary fixed fees.

Operational ask: if you choose OUR, please include the redwood_wire_instructions_v2.pdf reference code in the payment reference and upload the MT103 to HubSpot after settlement. For urgent payments today, we can provisionally accept a faxed confirmation from the sender bank but final reimbursement requires the MT103.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Collections, Redwood Inference
